items.stem: Why is the Polars expression API preferred over row-by-row Python loops?

options.text: Expressions run in parallel, vectorised native code and enable query optimisation
options.rationale: Correct: column expressions let Polars optimise and parallelise work.

options.text: Loops are not supported in Python
options.rationale: Loops exist; they are just slower here.

options.text: Expressions change the data types automatically to strings
options.rationale: Expressions do not force string types.
Polars runs on CPU; no GPU is required.

items.explanation: Correct: column expressions let Polars optimise and parallelise work.

items.stem: Which statements about Polars lazy evaluation are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A lazy query is only executed when collect() is called
options.rationale: Correct: lazy frames defer computation until collect().

options.text: The optimiser can push filters down to reduce scanned data
options.rationale: Correct: predicate pushdown reads less data.

options.text: Lazy frames execute each operation immediately
options.rationale: That describes eager mode, not lazy.
Joins work in lazy mode too.

items.explanation: Correct: lazy frames defer computation until collect().; Correct: predicate pushdown reads less data.

items.stem: When would you choose a left join over an inner join?

options.text: When you must keep all rows from the left frame even if there is no match on the right
options.rationale: Correct: a left join preserves unmatched left rows with nulls on the right.

options.text: When you want only rows present in both frames
When you want to remove duplicate keys
options.rationale: Deduplication is a separate operation from join type.

options.text: When the frames have no common key
options.rationale: A join still requires a key; this does not describe left vs inner.

items.explanation: Correct: a left join preserves unmatched left rows with nulls on the right.
